de31_watchdogs.topic: Inspectors general removed 2025; Storch v. Hegseth; precedent 2009/2020/2022/2024

claims.text: About 17 inspectors general were dismissed by email effective immediately on the night of Friday 24 January 2025; Congress did not receive the 30-day notice; Grassley: 'the 30 day detailed notice of removal that the law demands was not provided to Congress' and 'There may be good reason the IGs were fired. We need to know that if so.'; Warren: 'a purge of independent watchdogs in the middle of the night'

Judge Ana Reyes, 24 September 2025: 'President Trump violated the IGA. That much is obvious'; denied injunction restoring the eight plaintiff IGs (no irreparable harm; the president could re-fire after proper notice); left back pay open pending Slaughter; 'deserved better from their government. They still do.'
DOJ attorney at March 2025 hearing: 'we don't dispute that the president did not comply with the sentence in the statute', arguing the law does not require prior notice

Storch v. Hegseth stayed 25 Sep 2025 pending Slaughter; joint status report 13 Jul 2026; 20 Jul 2026 minute order set pre-motion conference for summary judgment (requests due 3 Aug, conference week of 24 Aug 2026); no ruling on the merits shown on the docket as of late October 2026
Obama removed AmeriCorps/CNCS IG Gerald Walpin in June 2009, saying he had 'lost confidence'; Grassley questioned whether the 30-day notice requirement was met

December 2022 amendments (P.L. 117-263) require a 'substantive rationale, including detailed and case-specific reasons' for IG removal; first tests were Biden's notices for the Railroad Retirement Board IG (29 March 2024) and Commerce acting IG (1 May 2024); Grassley argued the RRB notice lacked detail; in 2020 Trump replaced several IGs including those at Defense and the intelligence community

CIGIE FY2024 data: all federal IGs reported about $71bn in monetary impact against a $3.9bn budget (about 18:1); Sen. Peters's May 2025 report said the 19 fired IGs had identified $175bn in potential savings on open recommendations; the comparison with DOGE depends on which DOGE figure is used

de31_purse.topic: Spending control: GAO ICA findings, pocket rescission, Supreme Court stay; precedent Ukraine 2019 and Biden wall pause 2021

claims.text: GAO decision B-337204 (29 Sep 2025) found FEMA violated the ICA, 'The burden to justify withholdings rests with FEMA'; the Senate Appropriations minority listed it as GAO's seventh ICA violation finding of 2025: EV charging (May), museum and library (June), Head Start (July), K-12 energy efficiency (July), NIH (August), FEMA FY2025 and FEMA FY2021-24 (September)
GAO B-331564, 16 January 2020: 'OMB violated the ICA when it withheld USAI funds for a policy reason'; 'not a programmatic delay'
GAO, 15 June 2021: Biden's pause of more than $1 billion in border wall funds was a 'programmatic delay', not an impoundment; Shelby and Capito said it showed 'two sets of rules'

Pocket rescission special message 28 Aug 2025, nearly $5 billion in foreign aid expiring 30 Sep; OMB: Congress 'considered the possible effects of withholding funds close to the end of the fiscal year'; GAO B-330330.1: section 1012(b) 'may not lawfully be used to effect a pocket recission'; presidents of both parties have withheld funds proposed for rescission

Supreme Court, 26 Sep 2025, unsigned order: ICA likely precluded the recipients' suit; 'the asserted harms to the Executive's conduct of foreign affairs appear to outweigh the potential harm'; about $4bn of the $4.9bn; Kagan (with Sotomayor, Jackson): 'effectively altered the balance of power between Congress and the president over the power of the purse'; Vought: 'major victory'

de31_emergency.topic: Emergency powers: IEEPA tariffs, Section 122 and 301 replacement, congressional votes; Biden v. Nebraska precedent

claims.text: Court of International Trade, 7 May 2026, 2-1: the Section 122 10% global tariff proclamation exceeded presidential authority; relief limited to plaintiff importers and Washington State; DOJ appealed 8 May and the Federal Circuit granted a temporary stay 12 May; about $166bn of IEEPA duties being refunded through CBP's CAPE system, phase 1 from late April 2026

The Section 122 tariff expired 24 July 2026 and was replaced the same day by 'Forced Labor Tariffs' of 10-12.5% on goods from 60 economies under Section 301, said to cover 99% of US imports with exemptions

Senate, 29 Oct 2025, 50-46, passed a resolution to terminate the national emergency behind the Canada tariffs; Republicans Murkowski, Collins, McConnell and Paul joined Democrats; a Brazil resolution passed 28 Oct; House Republican rules let leaders block such votes

House, 11 Feb 2026, 219-211 with six Republicans, voted to end the Canada tariff emergency; Bacon: 'We should defend our authorities'; Hassett: 'The president will make sure they don't repeal his tariffs'

Biden v. Nebraska, 30 June 2023, 6-3: the HEROES Act, invoked on the COVID-19 national emergency, did not authorise the student-loan plan (more than $430bn principal, 40 million borrowers); the Secretary cannot 'rewrite the statute from the ground up'

de31_removal.topic: Removal power: bipartisan precedent (Biden's removal of SSA commissioner Saul, 2021)

claims.text: On 9 July 2021 President Biden removed Social Security Commissioner Andrew Saul, whose statute allowed removal only for cause; an OLC opinion the same day, relying on Collins v. Yellen and Seila Law, said 'the statutory restriction on removing the commissioner is unconstitutional'; Saul: 'I consider myself the term-protected Commissioner of Social Security'

EO 14215 (18 Feb 2025): independent agencies' significant rules go to OIRA before publication (FEC included); OMB sets performance standards and may adjust apportionments; White House liaisons; Sec. 7: the President's and AG's legal opinions 'are controlling on all employees' and no employee may advance a contrary legal position without written authorisation; the Fed's monetary policy excepted, the Board covered only for supervision and regulation

de31_data.topic: Data-sharing brakes loosened: CFPB data-broker rule withdrawal; industry response

claims.text: The CFPB withdrew its proposed rule 'Protecting Americans From Harmful Data Broker Practices (Regulation V)' (published 13 December 2024) effective 15 May 2025, citing 'updates to Bureau policies', 'its changed policy objectives', commenters' concerns and 'questions as to the Bureau's statutory authority'

CDIA president Dan Smith (14 May 2025): 'We appreciate CFPB Acting Director Russel Vought's leadership in recognizing the concerns we flagged'; said the rule 'did not align with the plain text of the Fair Credit Reporting Act'

de31_blocked.topic: What was blocked: CASA narrowing, AI moratorium stripped 99-1

claims.text: Trump v. CASA, 27 June 2025, 6-3 (Barrett): universal injunctions 'likely exceed the equitable authority that Congress has granted to federal courts'; class actions, APA vacatur and state relief left open; a New Hampshire court certified a class and enjoined the birthright-citizenship order class-wide on 10 July 2025; CRS counted 34 nationwide injunctions against the second administration from 20 Jan to 27 June 2025; Harvard Law Review counts 6 Bush, 12 Obama, 64 Trump-1, 14 in Biden's first three years

Senate on 1 July 2025 voted 99-1 to strip a 10-year state AI-law moratorium from the reconciliation bill; amendment by Markey (D), Cantwell (D) and Blackburn (R); it would have tied states' AI enforcement to BEAD broadband money
